acceptance_criteria.criterion: getGitStatus() returns a complete GitStatusInfo object with all fields populated
localCommits correctly counts commits ahead of upstream; returns 0 when no upstream is configured
unfetchedCommits correctly counts commits behind remote; returns 0 when no remote tracking
modifiedFiles correctly counts files shown in git status --porcelain
lastActivity returns an ISO 8601 string for repos with commits, and null for empty repos
hasConflicts correctly detects merge conflict markers in porcelain output
fetchAndGetStatus() calls fetchRemote() before gathering status, and still returns status even if fetch fails

summary: Created src/git/git-status.ts with getGitStatus() and fetchAndGetStatus() functions.

Updated GitStatusInfo in src/git/git.types.ts to match plan spec: replaced ahead/behind/isClean/modifiedFiles(array)/untrackedFiles with currentBranch/localCommits/unfetchedCommits/modifiedFiles(number)/lastActivity/hasConflicts.
All 7 git queries run in parallel via Promise.all in getGitStatus() for performance.
fetchAndGetStatus() calls fetchRemote() via a try/catch so fetch failures are swallowed and status is always returned.
Created src/tests/git-status.test.ts with 19 tests covering all 7 acceptance criteria; all 222 suite tests pass.

comments.note: The original GitStatusInfo in git.types.ts (set in WP-001) defined fields (ahead, behind, isClean, modifiedFiles as string[], untrackedFiles) that directly contradict the plan spec. The WP-001 implementation deviated from the plan's type definition. This required an AC-breaking change to the type. No downstream consumers existed yet so the impact was zero, but this kind of drift between the plan spec and the implementation is a risk for future WPs — consider adding a type-audit step to QA.

git-status.ts runs all five git sub-commands in a single Promise.all(), which is optimal for read-only queries. However, the porcelain result is parsed twice (once for modifiedFiles count, once for hasConflicts). Extracting a shared parse step would eliminate the duplication, though it is minor.

CONFLICT_CODES in git-status.ts is a module-level constant Set. This is correct and efficient. Worth noting that 'both added' (AA) and 'both deleted' (DD) codes are included — these are less common but valid conflict states that some implementations miss.

summary: Reviewed 3 modified files (git-status.ts, git.types.ts, git-status.test.ts) and 2 key dependencies (git-cli.ts, git-branch.ts). 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A03 (Injection) — CLEAR. git-cli.ts uses spawn('git', args, { shell: false }) on all invocations. In git-status.ts all git argument arrays are fully hardcoded; the repoPath parameter is passed exclusively as the cwd option and never interpolated into a git argument. No injection surface exists.

A09 (Security Logging) — LOW. fetchAndGetStatus() silences fetch errors via .catch(() => undefined) (git-status.ts, fetchAndGetStatus function). If git fetch fails due to authentication rejection or network error, the failure is not logged anywhere. For a developer-tool context this is acceptable by design, but it makes auth failure diagnosis harder. Consider logging the error at debug level.

A01 (Broken Access Control) — LOW/INFO. getGitStatus() and fetchAndGetStatus() accept a repoPath string with no path validation (e.g. no check that the path is within expected workspace boundaries). Since repoPath is sourced from internal workspace configuration rather than direct user input, exploitation risk is minimal in current architecture. If the API surface expands to accept user-supplied paths in future, path validation should be added.

summary: Code review complete — PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. git-status.ts, git.types.ts, and git-status.test.ts are well-structured, follow existing project patterns, and have thorough test coverage (19 tests, all AC met). Architecture is clean: Promise.all parallelism for read-only queries, shared porcelain parse step, correct conflict-code set, and silent fetch-failure behavior aligned with spec. One trivial non-behavioral improvement applied directly (see reviewer-applied-fix comment). No blocking issues found.

comments.note: src/git/git-status.ts — eliminated the redundant `lastActivityRaw` intermediate variable. The original two-step pattern `const lastActivityRaw = ...; const lastActivity = lastActivityRaw || null;` was consolidated into `const lastActivity = logResult.exitCode === 0 ? logResult.stdout.trim() || null : null;`. Semantically identical — the `|| null` coercion handles the edge case where exitCode is 0 but stdout is empty — but removes an unnecessary variable. Non-behavioral change.

src/git/git-status.ts — the JSDoc for `modifiedFiles` inside getGitStatus() says 'total lines returned by git status --porcelain'. The git.types.ts field comment is more precise ('Number of entries reported by git status --porcelain (staged, unstaged, and untracked)'). The JsDoc wording could cause a reader to conflate file count with raw line count. Minor but worth aligning.

[documentation-forward] src/tests/git-status.test.ts creates temp repos under os.tmpdir() without any cleanup (no after() hook, no process.on('exit') handler). The test suite should document whether this is intentional (relying on OS tmp cleanup) or an oversight. If intentional, add a comment near buildFixture(); if an oversight, add a cleanup step. The same pattern may apply to other test files in src/tests/.
